contradict_criteria: Paired profiler comparison shows no reproducible difference in stalls, bandwidth, or occupancy between baseline and trusted implementations on the focus workload, or any difference is within run-to-run variation.
correctness_plan: Retain existing FP16 reference PASS criteria for reviewed implementations; any follow-on change must re-pass the same reference check without altering tolerance.
difference_from_previous: This profiles the already-reviewed baseline, mask-hoisted, and two-slab implementations on the focus shape instead of proposing another K-loop or mask-hoisting source change.
expected_performance_mechanism: No speedup is claimed; a reproducibly measured stall or throughput limiter, if observed, could motivate a later targeted optimization.
measurement_plan: Run bounded profiler collection on the focus shape separately from paired CUDA-event screening; keep each screening ratio paired within its saved run and do not pool absolute times across runs.
optimization_mechanism: Profile existing reviewed kernels to locate a measured bottleneck before another transformation
reasoning_from_evidence: Measured screening deltas are within paired noise: trusted-compute median 1.002 with paired MAD 0.041 and AA deviation 0.038, and two-slab median 0.947 with AA deviation 0.048. Compiler shows identical registers and shared memory for trusted-compute versus doubled shared memory and higher registers for two-slab on the same workload, which does not establish overlap or stalls. The bottleneck is a prediction to test, not an established finding.
research_question: Which reproducibly measured profiler bottleneck distinguishes baseline from reviewed mask-hoisted and two-slab kernels on 512x3072x768 FP16?
risks_and_uncertainties: Profiling perturbs execution and does not establish latency or speedup.
Profiler counters have separate run-to-run variation from CUDA-event screening noise.
Conclusions scope only to the tested implementations, configuration, workload, and method.
support_criteria: A reproducible paired profiler observation identifies a specific stall, occupancy, or memory-throughput limiter to test on the focus workload.

supporting_evidence.why_relevant: Supplies near-parity screening within noise and identical compiled resources for the reviewed mask-hoisting implementation on the focus shape.
Supplies screening loss with increased registers and doubled shared memory for the reviewed two-slab implementation on the same focus shape.

technical_hypothesis: Unmeasured overlap or scheduling stalls may explain near-parity screening; targeted profiling may reveal the limiter to guide a future experiment.
